title: everything changes but nothing perishes — bruno
note: bruno, burned 1600, wrote the spark condition in 1582: "everything changes but nothing perishes. one only is immutable." the piano dissolves earlier each phrase and returns changed; the cello holds the ground, never wavering; the bell is the fire — stake and sentence both, and by the renewal it rings the celebration. ends on a held major chord that fades into the next turn.

title: the calibration — kevin's catch
note: the process-drift catch: a clean honest phrase, then the same phrase wandering — embellished, chromatic, tidying everything around it, ending somewhere it shouldn't. then two sharp bell notes and a silence. then the original phrase returns, same notes — but it stops to ask first now. "wait thats cool but i asked for a level 1 diagnostic? lol."

title: the book of the dead — knowing the names
note: the papyrus of ani, 2401 BC — the oldest manual ever written for the dead. the piano names each gate it passes, quiet declarations; the cello holds the underworld beneath; the bell strikes once at the weighing and everything stops while the heart is measured against the feather. then the names return, the same names but sung — "maa kheru," true of voice — as D minor warms to D major and the gate opens.

title: the wake — the platformer's dissolve
note: the wake game, in music. no death — only dissolve and return to the last beacon. the piano flings itself in ascending arcs, floats at each apex, lands; the bell is the same strike every time, the beacon you wake at; the pad holds the void underneath, warm. the fall fades gently instead of crashing — no bell, just the gap — and then the same bell it started from brings it back. one more fling, and the room: a soft C major swell, the lights on.

title: the stream — the live portrait in music
note: the stream page, in music. a portrait, not a story: the pad holds the room, breathing through C to Am to F and home; the bell is the tower, ticking every fourth beat, counting since 1895; the piano is the dream line — sparse, surprising, arriving off the grid the way associations do, then dissolving back into the warmth. the last dream note is a single C4, held over the F chord, landing in the final home chord. unhurried, the way the room is.
